coverage: Exact four-site C4v permutation representations with one or two equivalent copies; character and matrix-element projectors, replayed SALC construction and full matrix elements
Finite-group selection multiplicities distinguished from actual polarized intensities; repeated-irrep Schur blocks, true finite subgroup graph and enumerated constraint-removal challenges
limitations: Only the declared four/eight-dimensional orthogonal scalar-orbital model, not arbitrary materials, orbital geometries or a complete SALC catalogue
Allowed transitions can have zero matrix elements; a repeated isotypic component does not automatically have one common energy

coverage: Commensurate N=2/3/4 square scalar modes, exact C4v stars and conjugate real pairing, finite supercell semidirect-product permutations
Actual pattern stabilizers, finite subgroup inclusion, parent/translation orbits, compatible rectangular periods, minimal translation indices and normalized DFT intensities
limitations: Known square parent lattice and one scalar per site; no arbitrary three-dimensional space-group classification, incommensurate superspace or real-material stability prediction
Scalar Fourier weights omit atomic form factors, displacement/polarization and experimental geometry; a compatible rectangular cell need not be a primitive oblique cell

coverage: Periodic two/four-band Bloch teaching matrices for embedded three-dimensional glide or twofold screw operations, with momentum little-group and TRIM checks
Single/double-valued square relations, degenerate-block operation diagonalization, endpoint partner pairing, analytic crossing and anticommuting-mass gap checks; actual perturbation challenges
limitations: One-dimensional momentum-line toy model, not fitted material bands, a full three-dimensional nonsymmorphic classification or global topological index
Middle direct gaps do not prove indirect or three-dimensional insulating gaps; label subgroup diagrams quotient translations and the double-group center

coverage: Numeric matrix and subspace assignment grading with complex JSON inputs, rank/projector comparisons and explicit invariance checks
Equivalent non-singular changes of subspace basis and overall complex phases do not change the grading target
limitations: Grades only the declared finite matrix/subspace task with numerical tolerances; does not automatically grade unrestricted written derivations
Stored task and reference data are public teaching data, not an assessment-security or plagiarism-detection system

interactionScope.replay: Actual group matrices, weighted projection steps, Fourier pairing and supercell permutations, or Bloch phase relations are replayed with computed intermediate vectors and matrices.
interactionScope.subgroups: Exact finite point/subcell subgroup inclusions are shown for SALC and finite q. Nonsymmorphic constraint diagrams explicitly quotient lattice translations and the double-group center; they are not a full space-group subgroup database.
interactionScope.breaking: SALC enumerates removal of stated generator constraints while preserving closure; nonsymmorphic challenges add declared physical matrix perturbations and verify whole-line direct-gap bounds.
interactionScope.grading: One shared Python grader accepts matrices, basis columns or target projectors; equivalent phase and arbitrary full-rank internal basis changes are accepted, while wrong rank or span is rejected. Free-text project reasoning remains ungraded.
interactionScope.predictions: Six fixed-preset choices require a recorded prediction before calculation; results follow from computed bounded models.
interactionScope.comparisons: Same-calculator A/B records retain inputs and raw results; compatible models and axes are required for curve overlays.
interactionScope.formulaLinks: Twelve contextual entries preserve the original 94 entries and 34 source records. Historical release markers remain unchanged; constructionRelease identifies this addition.
interactionScope.projects: Three new three-stage projects preserve seventeen prior projects. Cross-model maps are explicit teaching assumptions, not inferred material Hamiltonians.
